citation.title: Deuterium charge exchange recombination spectroscopy from the top of the pedestal to the scrape off layer in H-mode plasmas
citation.authors: S. R. Haskey, B. A. Grierson, L. Stagner, K. Burrell, C. Chrystal, R. J. Groebner, A. Ashourvand, N. A. Pablant
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.1088/1748-0221/12/10/C10013 (from the supplied record's identifier hint; this DOI is not printed in the extracted text)

topic: Edge main-ion (Dα) CER on DIII-D, interpreted with iterative FIDAsim forward modeling, compared with C6+ impurity CER in the H-mode pedestal.
own_question: Can the deuterium temperature and rotation in the pedestal be recovered from Dα CER, and how do they differ from carbon-impurity values?
actual_method_and_evidence: The 16 edge chords have about 8 mm spacing and are typically run at 2.5 ms; the fastest stated acquisition is 0.2 ms. The thermal Dα feature is isolated with a multi-component spectral fit. Apparent values are corrected by iterating FIDAsim with additive residual updates, typically in fewer than 5 iterations. The authors state this offline correction takes about 4 hours per timeslice. The evidence is one low-power DIII-D discharge (#164436 at 4400 ms). In it, the D+ temperature is lower than C6+ at the separatrix, deuterium edge rotation is about twice the carbon rotation, and the carbon notch near rho 0.97 is absent in D+. No statistical validation is reported.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Reported CES temperature is a diagnostic-specific, model-processed quantity; impurity Ti can differ from main-ion Ti in the pedestal.
claim_checks.qualification: Shown for one DIII-D discharge, carbon versus deuterium. This is not KSTAR data and does not establish a general magnitude.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Some CES analyses involve spectral fitting plus forward modeling that is far from real time, which motivates distinguishing report availability from the plasma state.
claim_checks.qualification: The roughly 4 h per timeslice applies to the authors' main-ion edge pipeline, not to conventional C6+ CES. It is not a report-arrival measurement.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Acquisition is 2.5 ms (0.2 ms at fastest). Analysis is offline. No latency or arrival times are reported.
validation_if_relevant: Iteration convergence is checked against varied starting profiles in one shot. There is no independent ground truth and no held-out data.
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat KSTAR carbon CES reports as main-ion Ti.
Do not claim the KSTAR CES latency is about 4 h.
Do not generalize the one-shot discharge differences to all pedestals.
Do not describe this paper as prior nowcasting or real-time work.
Do not say our labels are physical truth because forward modeling exists.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: The paper supports the caveat that conventional C6+ CES labels are impurity-specific, model-dependent reports and not bulk-ion truth. It is useful for the theory and labels discussion, not as a methods comparator.
